A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CoMEM research. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices A–E are readable and support a reliable comparison after matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark evaluations, compression and long-context experiments, transfer results, and appendix training-efficiency analyses and case studies.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results in Sections 2 and 4 and Appendices D–E.

M1.justification: The VLM encoder, shared-parameter Q-Former, eight embeddings per knowledge item, LoRA training, and frozen downstream model remain unchanged. The added cache-KV caption documents the preliminary experiment without establishing a procedural change.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same training sources, WIT retrieval corpus, six English evaluation benchmarks, CVQA, translated InfoSeek, and multilingual coverage. Appendices A–E introduce no additional datasets or test scenarios.

E2.justification: The experimentally evaluated comparator sets remain unchanged. KV-Distill, M+, and MemGPT enter the descriptive related-work comparison, without reported benchmark evaluations against CoMEM; RoRA-VLM was already evaluated in v1.

E3.justification: The model configurations, training settings, retrieval procedures, validation splits, and evaluation metrics are retained. The long-context retrieval sweep and appendix data/parameter scaling protocols also remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The compression-rate study, long-context analysis, LLM transfer study, training-efficiency variations, and two appendix cases are retained. The new introductory diagram reuses the existing Lloyd’s Building case rather than adding a case study.

E5.justification: Neither version reports random seeds, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, or statistical significance tests. The uncertainty-reporting practice is unchanged.

E6.justification: The training-free results in v1 Table 1 and v2 Table 2 match, as do Tables 3–6, both experimental plots, and the appendix case answers. For example, Table 3 retains CoMEM averages of 38.7 and 35.4 for Qwen2-VL and Qwen2.5-VL.

T1.justification: The task formulation, Q-Former recursion in Equation 1, and memory-concatenation formulation are unchanged. No new assumptions, derivations, guarantees, or proofs are introduced.

C1.justification: The central claims remain VLMs serving as their own memory encoders, efficient training using 1.2% of parameters and 15.6K samples, eight-embedding compression, and plug-and-play multimodal/multilingual use. The rewritten conclusion preserves these contributions.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning semantic alignment, compressibility, multilingual transfer, and long-context stability are retained. Appendix C preserves the same limitations concerning static benchmarks, dynamic or noisy inputs, and unexplored multi-agent use.

D1.justification: The expanded caption of v2 Table 2 explicitly identifies the preliminary memory as cached keys/values from an unfine-tuned VLM and distinguishes it from Section 3’s trained method. Existing implementation details, hyperparameters, hardware, training time, and code/data access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The descriptive comparison expands from six related methods in v1 Table 2 to ten in v2 Table 1, adding RoRA-VLM, KV-Distill, M+, and MemGPT. The latter three are newly cited works; the broad positioning around continuous memory, compression, and multimodal RAG remains intact.

P1.justification: v2 rewrites the conclusion, makes localized language corrections, expands the preliminary-experiment caption, and updates the comparative discussion. The main section structure and appendices remain unchanged.

P2.justification: v2 adds an introductory CoMEM-versus-RAG schematic and expands and relocates the related-work table with category labels and fuller headings. Existing figures and tables are renumbered, repositioned, or resized, while their experimental content is retained.

improvement.justification: v2 improves clarity through the explicit distinction between the preliminary cache-KV experiment and trained CoMEM, an introductory schematic, and a broader related-work comparison. These are useful but limited gains: the method, experimental evidence, and appendix analyses remain unchanged.
